memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day. - Gen 1:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sixth day comes to a close, and with it, God's great work of creation. Throughout the chapter, God has paused again and again to call His work "good." But now, looking over the whole of it, humanity included, He says something more: it was "very good." The finished creation, complete and full, brought Him deep delight.

Take a moment to feel the weight of this. When everything came fresh from God's hand, there was no sin, no death, no sorrow, no brokenness. Everything was exactly as He intended, whole and beautiful and good. This is the world as God designed it, and it tells us that goodness, not evil, is the deepest truth about God's creation.

We do not live in that unbroken world now. Sin entered, and with it came all the pain and struggle we know. But this verse reminds us of where we came from, and it whispers of where God is taking us. For God is making all things new, and there is coming a day when His people will dwell in a creation once again free from every tear (Rev 21:4-5).

The One through whom all things were made is the One who will restore all things (Col 1:20). The "very good" of creation points forward to the "very good" of the new creation in Christ. Rest today in the goodness of your God, who made all things well, and who is making all things new.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does knowing God's original creation was "very good" shape the way you see the world?
2. Does the hope of God making all things new bring you comfort today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You made all things very good, and You are making all things new in Christ. Thank You for Your goodness. Fill me with hope as I trust Your restoring work. Amen.
